svg.text: Fan speed follows the zone: red (≤ 5 cm) = fan stops · blue (5-15 cm) = fast · green (> 15 cm) = slow · pins: same wiring as v1 (assumed; not visible in footage)
Fan driver = RECOMMENDED parts (TIP120, 1N4007, 4×AA): the driver on the original breadboard is not legible in the recordings.
speed: stop / fast / slow (PWM on D11)
Build it in this order — numbers match the white circles on the wires
LED long leg (+) column 12, short leg 13
Blue LED (medium) — yellowLed in the code
LED long leg (+) column 22, short leg 23
LED long leg (+) column 32, short leg 33
1 kΩ across the centre gap, column 50
TIP120 printed side toward you: B=50, C=51, E=52
motor: black lead column 51, red lead 55
* Recommended, not seen: an Uno pin gives 20 mA, a propeller motor needs a few hundred mA, so the pin only drives the TIP120 (via 1 kΩ ≈ 3.6 mA) and the transistor switches the motor.
The 1N4007 catches the motor's switch-off voltage spike. The motor runs from its own battery; only the grounds are joined. Match the battery to your motor's rated voltage.
Speed = analogWrite(D11, …): stop / fast / slow values are set at the top of final-fan.ino. A logic-level MOSFET (e.g. IRLZ44N) can replace the TIP120. Top rails are not used.
